title: Collective Mining Intersects High-Grade Gold Outside the Mineral Resource in Apollo’s Eastern Shallow Halo Zone, Including 14.25 m @ 6.49 g/t AuEq* and 67.25 m @ 1.58 g/t AuEq*
summary: Miami, Florida, October 27, 2026 – Collective Mining Ltd. (NASDAQ: CNL; TSX: CNL) (“Collective” or the “Company”) is...
body_markdown:
- **Holes drilled from Pad43 in the eastern Shallow Halo Zone (“SHZ”) intersected high-grade gold outside the Mineral Resource:**


- **14.25 m @ 6.49 g/t AuEq (5.49 g/t Au, 52 g/t Ag) from 81.60 m, including 3.60 m @ 18.83 g/t AuEq (16.19 g/t Au, 136 g/t Ag) from 90.60 m in APC-218**


- **67.25 m @ 1.58 g/t AuEq (1.07 g/t Au, 26 g/t Ag) from 95.00 m, including 19.70 m @ 4.42 g/t AuEq (2.88 g/t Au, 80 g/t Ag) from 117.70 m in APC-204**


- **APC-226 intersected broad near-surface mineralization in the northern SHZ (Pad35), returning 197.40 m @ 0.74 g/t AuEq (0.26 g/t Au, 21 g/t Ag, 0.07% Cu) from 2.85 m, including 30.55 m @ 2.02 g/t AuEq (0.37 g/t Au, 83 g/t Ag, 0.04% Cu) from 25.50 m in oxide rock.**


- **In the southeastern SHZ (Pad42), APC-200 returned 4.70 m @ 12.00 g/t AuEq (2.20 g/t Au, 506 g/t Ag) from 134.70 m within 15.80 m @ 3.78 g/t AuEq (0.72 g/t Au, 158 g/t Ag) from 124.80 m, and APC-183 returned 16.50 m @ 2.06 g/t AuEq (1.77 g/t Au, 15 g/t Ag) from 3.10 m.**


- **Of the 24 SHZ holes reported in this release, 22 returned mineralized intervals above the open-pit cut-off grade of 0.30 g/t AuEq. Since the Mineral Resource announcement on September 8, 2026, a total of 44 out of 47 SHZ holes have returned mineralized intervals exceeding this cut-off grade, with much of the mineralization occurring outside the current Mineral Resource. To date, approximately 41% of the SHZ area has been drill tested with two rigs currently dedicated to testing the remaining 59%.**


- **Assays are pending for 69 holes at the Guayabales Project, including 23 from the SHZ and 21 from the Ramp Zone. With 13 rigs turning, the Company is fully funded for its planned 2026 drilling program.**


- **APC-218: 6.49 g/t AuEq (5.49 g/t Au and 52 g/t Ag). APC-204: 1.58 g/t AuEq* *(1.07 g/t Au and 26 g/t Ag).*


**Miami, Florida, October 27, 2026 – Collective Mining Ltd. (NASDAQ: CNL; TSX: CNL) (“Collective” or the “Company”)** is pleased to announce assay results for thirty diamond drill holes from its 2026 fully funded drilling program at the Guayabales Project in Caldas, Colombia. Twenty-four holes targeted the Shallow Halo Zone (“SHZ”) of the Apollo deposit (“Apollo”), five holes tested areas outside the southern limit of the SHZ, and one geotechnical hole, GTC-4, intersected high-grade gold veins at depth. The SHZ is an interpreted 2.4-kilometer-long, 200-meter-wide, precious-metal-dominant target area which currently lies within the Mineral Resource open pit shell and, based on surface sampling, potentially extends well beyond the pit shell.


The results announced today follow the Company’s September 8, 2026, announcement of the maiden Mineral Resource for Apollo and its October 13, 2026, release of seventeen SHZ holes, and continue to test one of the key areas for potential future Mineral Resource growth at Apollo. This release extends drilling coverage of the SHZ to the east and southeast of the Apollo Breccia from two new drill pads, Pad43 and Pad42.


**Ari Sussman, Executive Chairman, commented:** “Mineral systems of this scale reveal themselves in layers. Apollo’s high-grade core drew the market’s attention first, but the shallow halo surrounding it is now telling its own story: widespread gold outside the Mineral Resourceat Pad43, broad mineralization from surface at Pad35 and silver-rich intervals at Pad42. With most of the halo zone still untested, and an exploration adit set to open the district to underground drilling, we believe we are still in the early chapters of the Guayabales Project’s growth.”


To date, Collective has received assays for **204,500 meters** of diamond drilling across the Guayabales and San Antonio projects, including results for **143,000 meters** at the flagship Apollo deposit, which anchors the Guayabales Project. Assay results for 69 drill holes are outstanding, including 23 from the SHZ and 21 from the Ramp Zone, covering approximately 25,000 meters of drilling.


With **US$93.7 million** in cash (as of June 30, 2026), the Company is fully funded for its planned **2026 program** , which envisions up to **90,000 meters** of drilling. The Company presently has 13 diamond drill rigs operating across the Guayabales Project. An updated Mineral Resource incorporating approximately 100,000 meters of additional drilling is expected in Q4 2027 to Q1 2028, followed by a Preliminary Economic Assessment shortly thereafter.


Construction of the approximately 3-kilometer underground exploration adit is scheduled to begin in Q4 2026. The adit is designed to provide underground drilling platforms, beginning with the Trap system in Q1 2027, followed by the Plutus target and ultimately the Ramp Zone at Apollo, while allowing the Company to test any additional mineralization intersected along its route. The Company is targeting the second half of 2027 to submit the environmental license application for Apollo to Colombia’s National Environmental Licensing Authority (Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales, “ANLA”).


**Drill Results and Geological Context (See Table 1 and Figures 1-3)**


Twenty-four diamond drill holes completed from Pad35, Pad43 and Pad42 tested Apollo’s SHZ, an interpreted 2.4-kilometer-long, 200-meter-wide, precious-metal-dominant target which currently lies within the Mineral Resource open pit shell. A further five holes were drilled from Pad45, outside the southern limit of the SHZ, and geotechnical hole GTC-4 intersected high-grade gold veins at depth. Potential extensions beyond the pit shell are planned to be tested by drilling in 2027.


The SHZ extends from surface to approximately 150 meters below surface and hosts mineralization in oxide, partially oxidized (transition) and primary rock. The zone of oxidation extends in places up to 125 meters below surface. Mineralization within the SHZ is intrusion-related and is characterized by disseminated sulfosalts and carbonate base metal veins.


Of the 24 SHZ holes, 22 returned intervals above the Mineral Resource cut-off grade for the open pit; APC-212 returned no significant values and APC-220 returned 10.50 meters at 0.27 g/t AuEq. Combined with the twenty-three SHZ holes announced on September 15 and October 13, 2026, 44 of the 47 SHZ holes reported since the Mineral Resource announcement have returned mineralization above the 0.30 g/t AuEq assumed cut-off grade. All interval starting depths reported below are down-hole.


**Northern SHZ – Pad35**


Four holes were drilled from Pad35, adding to the five holes reported from this pad on October 13, 2026. All four intersected broad zones of mineralization starting at or near surface, largely outside the current Mineral Resource. Results include:


**APC-226**


- **197.40 m @ 0.74 g/t AuEq (0.26 g/t Au, 21 g/t Ag, 0.07% Cu) from 2.85 meters**


- **Including 30.55 m @ 2.02 g/t AuEq (0.37 g/t Au, 83 g/t Ag, 0.04% Cu) from 25.50 meters in oxide rock**


**APC-223**


- **76.00 m @ 0.75 g/t AuEq (0.15 g/t Au, 28 g/t Ag, 0.06% Cu) from surface**


- **Including 16.00 m @ 2.11 g/t AuEq (0.26 g/t Au, 91 g/t Ag, 0.09% Cu) from 60.00 meters in transition rock**


- **1.05 m @ 4.19 g/t AuEq (1.30 g/t Au, 141 g/t Ag, 0.16% Cu) from 108.65 meters in primary rock**


**APC-219**


- **82.50 m @ 0.55 g/t AuEq (0.28 g/t Au, 11 g/t Ag, 0.05% Cu) from 1.50 meters**


- **Including 34.20 m @ 0.81 g/t AuEq (0.44 g/t Au, 17 g/t Ag, 0.05% Cu) from 28.50 meters in oxide rock**


**APC-216**


- **115.00 m @ 0.36 g/t AuEq (0.14 g/t Au, 9 g/t Ag, 0.05% Cu) from 0.40 meters**


- **Including 19.65 m @ 0.79 g/t AuEq (0.14 g/t Au, 31 g/t Ag, 0.05% Cu) from 79.20 meters in oxide rock**


**Eastern SHZ – Pad43**


Eleven holes were drilled in a fan pattern from Pad43, located approximately 525 meters south-southeast of Pad35 on the eastern margin of the current Mineral Resource. The holes intersected gold-dominant mineralization in oxide, transition and primary rock, associated with sulfosalts and sericite alteration under structural control, with several high-grade intervals outside the Mineral Resource. **Southeastern SHZ – Pad42**


Nine holes were drilled from Pad42, located approximately 130 meters south of Pad43. Eight of the nine holes returned mineralized intervals; APC-212 returned no significant values. Near-surface gold was intersected in oxide rock in several holes, while APC-200 intersected a silver-rich interval in transition rock associated with minor sulfosalts and sericite alteration, with a structural control similar to that observed at the northern pads. **Outside the Southern SHZ – Pad45**


Five holes were drilled from Pad45, located approximately 30 meters south of the SHZ outline, to test for a potential southern extension of the SHZ beyond its currently interpreted limit. Three of the five holes intersected modest mineralization, including near-surface gold in oxide rock, while two holes (APC-222 and APC-235) returned no significant values. Results include:

- **1.00 m @ 10.95 g/t AuEq (10.75 g/t Au, 4 g/t Ag, 0.12% Cu) from 53.00 meters in primary rock**


**APC-231**

**APC-228**


- **1.60 m @ 3.52 g/t AuEq (3.47 g/t Au, 3 g/t Ag) from 45.80 meters in oxide rock**


**High-Grade Gold Veins Outside the Southeastern Mineral Resource**


Several holes intersected high-grade gold veins at depth, outside the southeastern portion of the current Mineral Resource:


**APC-188**


- **19.05 m @ 5.48 g/t AuEq (5.28 g/t Au, 10 g/t Ag) from 388.95 meters**


- **Including 1.65 m @ 51.56 g/t AuEq (51.22 g/t Au, 18 g/t Ag) from 400.70 meters**


**GTC-4**


- **1.55 m @ 42.79 g/t AuEq (42.50 g/t Au, 15 g/t Ag) from 574.50 meters**


**APC-192**


- **1.00 m @ 9.76 g/t AuEq (8.93 g/t Au, 38 g/t Ag, 0.08% Cu) from 300.15 meters**


**Potential to Expand the SHZ Beyond the Current Mineral Resource**


As shown in Figure 1, a significant portion of the mineralized intervals reported from Pad35, Pad43 and Pad42 lies outside the current Mineral Resource and extends into previously undrilled areas. These results support the potential to add Mineral Resources within the existing open pit shell.


Exploration potential also extends beyond the open pit shell. Northern SHZ mineralization remains open to the north and east of Pad35, while large portions of the SHZ west, south and southeast of the Apollo Breccia remain undrilled.


At an elevation of 1,950 masl, approximately 41% of the interpreted SHZ area has been drill tested, leaving approximately 59% untested. Two rigs are dedicated to evaluating this remaining exploration potential.

**Notes**


1. Intervals are down-hole lengths. Estimated true widths range from 60% to 100% of reported intervals. Grades are uncut.
2. Included intervals fall within the preceding overall interval and do not necessarily represent its entire length.
3. **AuEq (g/t) = \[(Au × 0.95) + (Ag × 0.020 × 0.92) + (Cu × 1.20 × 0.85)\] ÷ 0.95, where Au and Ag are expressed in g/t, and Cu in percent.
4. The calculation uses metal prices of US$3,000/oz gold, US$60/oz silver and US$5.25/lb copper with assumed recoveries of 95%, 92%, and 85% respectively. Copper is included in AuEq where the intercept’s copper grade is 0.04% or higher. A hyphen (-) in the copper column indicates a grade below 0.04%.
5. Recovery assumptions are based on metallurgical results announced on August 25, 2026, and used in the maiden Mineral Resource announced on September 8, 2026.

**About Collective Mining Ltd.** ****


Founded by the team that developed and sold Continental Gold Inc. to Zijin Mining for approximately $1.4 billion in enterprise value, Collective is a gold, silver, copper and tungsten exploration company with projects in Caldas, Colombia. The Company’s two projects are located directly within an established mining camp with ten fully permitted and operating mines.


The Company’s flagship project, Guayabales, is anchored by Apollo, a large-scale, bulk-tonnage and high-grade gold-silver-copper-tungsten deposit that hosts a maiden Mineral Resource of 2.58 million ounces AuEq Indicated (37.0 Mt at a grade of 2.17 g/t AuEq) and 2.83 million ounces AuEq Inferred (48.2 Mt at a grade of 1.83 g/t AuEq). The Company’s objectives at the Guayabales Project are to continue expansion and infill drilling at Apollo while advancing technical, environmental and permitting work across the project.


Management, insiders, a strategic investor and close family and friends own 45.2% of the outstanding shares of the Company and, as a result, are fully aligned with shareholders. The Company is listed on both Nasdaq and the TSX under the trading symbol “CNL”.

**Technical Information** ****


Samples were cut by Company personnel at Collective Mining’s core facility in Caldas, Colombia. Diamond drill core was sawed and then sampled in maximum 2-meter intervals, stopping at geological boundaries. Drill hole core diameter is a mix of PQ, HQ and NQ depending on the depth of the drill hole. Core samples have been prepared and analyzed at ALS laboratory facilities in Medellin, Colombia and Lima, Peru for copper, gold and silver assays, and multi-element ICP. ALS is an accredited laboratory which is independent of the Company. Gold assays are obtained by fire assay fusion with AAS finish on a 50g sample (Au-AA24). Any samples returning > 10 g/t were then reanalyzed by fire assay with gravimetric finish on a 50g sample (Au-GRA22). Copper and silver were assayed by inductively coupled plasma – Atomic Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-AES) and Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) following a 4-acid digestion. Samples were also analyzed for a suite of 48 elements with ME-MS61 plus mercury and a sequential copper leach analysis was completed on each sample with copper greater than 10,000 parts per million. Blanks, duplicates, and certified reference standards are inserted into the sample stream to monitor laboratory performance. Crush rejects and pulps are kept and stored in a secured storage facility for future assay verification. No capping has been applied to sample composites. The Company utilizes a rigorous, industry-standard QA/QC program.
